clue.text: Get in by force, taking risks

parts.note: to get in somewhere is to enter it
prising is levering something open by force

explanation.surface: Someone breaks into a place forcibly, a risky business.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprising person shows initiative and boldness, ready to try a venture that might fail.

clue.text: For the record, it holds the title

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: holds says one piece of the clue wraps round the next, here it round the

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Speaking for the record, someone says this one is the champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' wraps 'it' round 'the'; 'For the record' reads like a speaker's aside but supplies the disc.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive name or byname attached to a person, a kind of honorific.

clue.text: Way to set up examinations

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on how to compose an exam paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole of ST + SET, giving TESTS (the run STSET read backwards).
explanation.definitionFit: Tests and examinations are synonyms: both are assessments of knowledge.

clue.text: Air aces in violent storm

indicators.note: violent suggests letters thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fighter pilots flying through a violent storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' rearranges AIRACESIN to give the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise Cain is an idiom for making an angry fuss, raging or storming about something.

clue.text: Bank on river with sea, we hear, below

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed below comes after the one above it

parts.note: sea sounds like see, a bishop's diocese, and Ely in Cambridgeshire is one

explanation.surface: Someone relies on a riverbank next to the sea, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone hint 'we hear' turns sea into see, a cathedral diocese; Ely, a cathedral city in eastern England, is such a see, and it goes under R.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to depend on or count on them.

clue.text: Deposit forwarded, investing money in America

indicators.note: investing in its old sense of clothing or surrounding, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: something forwarded has been sent on
a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: A payment forwarded after putting money into the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' has its old sense of enclosing; the money words 'investing' and 'Deposit' tempt a solver towards banking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles and is laid down at the bottom of a liquid.

clue.text: Agreeable to accept opening of House in recess

indicators.note: to accept means the word for agreeable takes a letter into itself

parts.note: agreeable means nice

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Willing to take a seat in the House while Parliament is in recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts H, from 'opening of House', inside NICE; 'recess' reads as a parliamentary break.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a shallow alcove set into a wall.

clue.text: Wine distributor supplying notes on list with hesitation

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: D and E are two musical notes
to list is to lean or tilt, as does cant
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A wine merchant gives tasting notes from the list, umming and erring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' is a ship's lean, not a catalogue; CANT also means tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel from which wine is poured out and served at the table.

clue.text: Some complaint endangers plan

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Any grievance can put a scheme at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to mean or aim to do it.

clue.text: Implanted in soil initially cultivated

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of soil

parts.note: tilled land has been ploughed and cultivated

explanation.surface: A plant has been put in the soil, which was dug over first.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to plant it gradually in someone's mind.

clue.text: Complete egghead in family group

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a clan is an extended family group
read as egg's head, the first letter of egg

explanation.surface: A thoroughly brainy academic within a family circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual, but it is the head of egg, E, placed 'in' CLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean in the sense of complete or total, as in a clean sweep or a clean break.

clue.text: Straying, he lost shelter

indicators.note: straying letters wander out of their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who wandered off and got lost found refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straying' rearranges HELOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostel provides cheap lodging and refuge for travellers or the homeless.

clue.text: French scientist comprehends silver's current strength

indicators.note: comprehends in its old sense of includes, so one piece takes in another

parts.note: Andre-Marie Ampere was the French physicist who gave his name to the unit of current
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A French physicist understands how well silver conducts electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehends' means includes, not understands; the unit of current is named after the scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Amperage is the size of an electric current measured in amps.

clue.text: Act about graduate's headgear

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a turn is an act in a variety show
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Someone performs while wearing a graduation cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the wrap; a turn is a music-hall or variety act.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a head covering made from a long cloth wound round the head.

clue.text: One selling or telling stories, perhaps

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper, or someone telling tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: a re-taler is someone who tells stories again.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a shopkeeper selling to the public; split as re-taler, it is one who recounts tales.

clue.text: A bad tune played without let up

indicators.note: played suggests notes performed in a new order, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A poor melody performed relentlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges ABADTUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabated means continuing with undiminished force, never easing off.

clue.text: Strand dance with bouncer

parts.note: a strand is a shore or beach
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Dancing on the Strand, with a nightclub doorman in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strand' looks like the London street but means shore; 'bouncer' looks like a doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: A large inflatable toy for the seaside, which bounces when thrown.

clue.text: Bound to be short of cash

explanation.surface: A person certain to end up broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped means fastened with a strap, and in slang, strapped for cash means hard up.

clue.text: Set off for school in time

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a date is a time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Leaving for school on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the wrap; 'Set off' looks like departing, but means explode.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to set it off.

clue.text: Testify to the Camptown attitude

parts.note: in the song Camptown Races, sung in dialect, the is sung as de
a pose is a stance or attitude

explanation.surface: Giving evidence about the folk song's attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Camptown Races is a US minstrel song beginning 'De Camptown ladies sing dis song'.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose is to give sworn evidence, especially in writing, in legal language.

clue.text: A growing incentive?

parts.note: an inducement dangled in front of a donkey that is also a root vegetable raised in the garden

explanation.surface: An incentive that keeps increasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing' reads as increasing, but means cultivated in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is both a root vegetable and a reward offered to encourage effort.

clue.text: Service men in river or fast stream

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
OR, other ranks, are servicemen who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers wading in a river, a fast-flowing stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the wrap; 'or' is a link before the definition, and the Trent is a river in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violently rushing flow of water.

clue.text: Indication of cost to refit carpeting if not new

indicators.note: to refit is to fit together again in a new arrangement
if not says the letter for new is left out

explanation.surface: A quote for refitting the carpet, if not buying a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if not' drops N from CARPETING, and 'to refit' rearranges the remaining CARPETIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A price tag is the label showing what an item costs.

clue.text: Provide with proper directions to start

indicators.note: to start means these letters come first, before the next piece

parts.note: E and N are compass directions, east and north
due means proper or fitting, as in due respect

explanation.surface: Give someone correct instructions to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' puts the compass points first; 'Provide with' is one phrasal definition, as in to endue someone with grace.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue someone with a quality is to endow or invest them with it.

clue.text: Individual in pursuit of one drink after another

explanation.surface: Someone hunting down one drink after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a pursuer, and also a drink taken straight after another, such as a beer after a whisky.

clue.text: Sent out notes about student's bad language?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to send out musical notes is to sing, so sang
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Someone sang a ditty about a student's foul language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside SANG; 'Sent out notes' looks like posting letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal, nonstandard vocabulary, often frowned on as poor usage.

clue.text: Article in support of little woman or girl

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece in support of another sits beneath it

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article backing a short woman or a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little woman' reads as a small lady, but points to Jo of Little Women; AN goes beneath her.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan is a female first name, and a girl's name stands for a girl in crosswords.

clue.text: Rate obtainable from 18 dn nonetheless

indicators.note: obtainable from says the letters can be got out by rearranging another word
read as none-less: without O, the round letter that stands for nothing

parts.note: the answer to 18 down

explanation.surface: A price that can be got from the other clue all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' drops O, which stands for none, from DEPOSE, and 'obtainable from' rearranges DEPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed is a rate of motion, distance covered per unit of time.

clue.text: Spread for a crowd on the shore

indicators.note: on the means the following pieces are placed after the one for the support

parts.note: to shore is to prop up, and a shore is a prop
a gate is the crowd attending a sports match

explanation.surface: A picnic laid out for a large gathering at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shore' looks like the seaside, but is a supporting beam; 'on the' places the article and crowd after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate is to spread or disseminate, as of ideas or plants.

clue.text: A prominent personage, 1 ac

explanation.surface: A notable figure, linked to the first answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a joke: 1 across is the first, or leading, light (entry) in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading light is an important, influential figure; 1 across is also literally the first light in the puzzle.
